chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and later years
title: Jazz at the Philharmonic with Ella Fitzgerald
summary: Edison names the 1950 JATP package with Ella, Pres, Hawkins and Buddy Rich, and praises Norman Granz.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Well, when did you work with Ella?
Oh, I worked with Ella in the Jazz at the Philharmonic in 1950.

Yeah, yeah. I had worked with her before around New York. Let's see, where did I work with her? I worked with her before that, but -- I worked with her for like six weeks with Jazz Philharmonic, you know. Ella Fitzgerald, Prez, Coleman Hawkins, Buddy Rich, Hank Jones, Ray Brown, Herb Ellis. No, didn't have a guitar. Hank Jones, Ray Brown and Bill Harris.
No, no, Bill Harris, trombone player.
Flip Phillips and myself. And Ella. And Oscar Peterson, and Oscar, yeah.
Yes. Hank was playing for Ella.

You see, he was playing for Ella. And we had -- the next time I went out was -- it was Louie Bellson, practically the same ones, you know, practically the same ones. But Herb Ellis, he didn't make those tours with us. But that was a fantastic time, real great. I think Norman puts on the finest sessions that can be put on, I really do.
Well, he has a very good idea of --
Yeah, well, he's been at it a long time.
